title: PickMe card catalogue
description: Documents the shape of card-catalogue.json exactly as decoded by Engine/Sources/CardCopilotEngine/Models/CatalogueModels.swift — it does not redesign the shape (spec §4). Two distinct 'unused' markers appear below: "x-status": "declared-not-computed" means the field IS a Swift struct property but no scoring/matching logic (RuleMatcher, Scorer, CapMath, PortfolioAnalyzer) ever reads it; "x-status": "documentation-only" means the field has NO corresponding Swift property at all, so JSONDecoder silently drops it on load — it is pure human-facing metadata. Two behaviors are engine-defined rather than data-defined: ownerConditions ids and the pseudo-categories/categoryParents RuleMatcher special-cases. This schema enumerates their current legal values; adding a new one is an engine code change, not a catalogue edit. program.programId used to be a third — the Scorer switched its valuation dispatch on that string — but since 2026-08-20 valuations are keyed data (programs.json, overridable per programId by owner state) and the Scorer dispatches on the valuation's model instead. 2.0 is the multi-market bump: every card now carries `market`/`billingCurrency`, monetary fields are `{amount, currency}` pairs instead of bare CAD numbers, and a `status` tier separates checkout-eligible products from research-grade drafts (see the top-level and cardProduct descriptions below).

catalogueVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR. Load-bearing: SeedLoader.validate(catalogueVersion:) parses MAJOR and throws SeedLoaderError.unsupportedCatalogueVersion if it isn't a MAJOR this build recognizes (currently only 2, bumped from 1 for the multi-market shape change — Money-shaped fees/credits, `market`/`billingCurrency`, `status`, `spendNative` replacing `spendCad`, `calendarQuarter`). Bump MAJOR on any breaking shape change, MINOR on additive/compatible ones; every edit gets a CHANGELOG.md entry (spec §3).

currency.description: The engine's fixed REPORTING currency — every CandidateScore/PortfolioAnalyzer/AcquisitionAnalyzer output number (netValueCad, annualFeeCad, ...) is expressed in this currency regardless of a card's own `market`/`billingCurrency` or a purchase's `currency`. Not per-card, and not a claim that every card bills in CAD — see cardProduct.billingCurrency for that. A non-CAD catalogue figure (a USD fee, a USD-valued program) is converted to this reporting currency at the point it is combined with one, via ReportingCurrency's pinned rate (Swift: Engine/Sources/CardCopilotEngine/Models/ReportingCurrency.swift) — never a live rate, consistent with this repo not owning market data (ECOSYSTEM.md).

_provenance.description: Free-text sourcing note. No Catalogue.provenance property exists in Swift.

programId.description: The key a card's rewards currency is valued under. Hoisted into $defs on 2026-08-20 so programs.schema.json can reference the one list instead of keeping a second copy in step. Since that date this is a DATA key, not an engine dispatch key: Scorer.valueCad switches on the valuation's model, so a new programId needs an entry in programs.json (or an owner-state override) and no engine code change. A programId with NEITHER has no valuation, and that is not inert: Scorer.valueCad answers nil/null and Scorer.score EXCLUDES every card on it with unsupportedProgram. It never scores zero — "we cannot value this" must not rank as "this is worth nothing", which is the distinction noRewards exists to make sayable. Several entries here are deliberately unvalued, and every card on one is therefore a `draft`: the six `*Us`/US-issuer entries added 2026-08-26 for the multi-market import, and the seven co-brand currencies added 2026-08-27 (catalogue 2.4) under the Option 2 follow-up to that day's Option 1 ruling. Do NOT read an entry's presence here as the programme being valued — check programs.json. Publishing a card on an unvalued programme makes it vanish from every recommendation rather than rank badly; CatalogueIntegrityTests.testEveryProgramIdIsValuedOrKnownUnvalued and CoBrandProgramTests.testEveryCardOnAnUnvaluedProgramIsADraft hold that line from both ends. `noRewards` is a card with no rewards programme at all (MBNA True Line, Capital One Guaranteed Secured). It is a STATED fact, not an absence: its valuation model answers 0.0 so the card is scored and ranks last on merit, where a missing valuation answers nil and excludes the card entirely. Same principle as fxRules, where a fee-free card declares rate 0.0 rather than saying nothing.

market.description: The country whose product this is — NOT the currency it bills in on its own (see billingCurrency) and not, by itself, an eligibility claim beyond "this is the market the card is sold in" (see cardProduct.eligibility.residency for the rare card sold in both). Closed enum: a third market is a deliberate scope decision (ECOSYSTEM.md's horizon), not a data entry, so an unrecognised value should fail loudly rather than decode silently.

currencyCode.description: The two currencies this catalogue represents. Every Money value and CardProduct.billingCurrency uses this vocabulary. Adding a third market's currency is a schema + engine change (Money.toReporting needs a rate for it), same reasoning as `market`.

money.description: Mirrors Swift's Money — a currency-tagged monetary figure. Replaces the old bare `annualCad`/`monthlyCad`/`valueCad` numbers, which assumed CAD unconditionally (Phase 1: 'a price without a currency must not be summed' applies here exactly as it does to Holding.priceCurrency in MoneyTalks). Never converted in place: a USD fee stays `{amount, currency: "USD"}` in the catalogue forever — conversion to the engine's CAD reporting currency happens at the point of use (PortfolioAnalyzer/AcquisitionAnalyzer), via ReportingCurrency's pinned rate, and is never written back into this field.

eligibility.description: Residency/offer-market facts, decoded where the field says so and documentation-only otherwise. Deliberately thin in this bump — only `residency` gates anything (AcquisitionAnalyzer). The rest are Phase-5-style capture points for a later pass; representing them as `unknown`-by-absence now (rather than inventing values) matches the catalogue's existing rule for CardCredit and FxRule provenance.

residency.description: Which market(s) a resident must be in to hold this card. Absent means "assume [market]" (AcquisitionAnalyzer.eligibleMarkets falls back to `[card.market]` when this is nil) — only set this when a card is sold to residents of a market other than its own `market`, which is rare enough that inventing a default beyond the card's own market would be a guess.

incomeRequirementCad.description: Personal/household income requirement, always expressed in the catalogue's CAD reporting currency regardless of market, for comparability. Not decoded in this bump — see card-research-queue.json for which cards still need it sourced.

provinceStateRestriction.description: e.g. Desjardins products restricted outside Quebec, or a US card unavailable in a given state.

cardProduct.description: Mirrors CardProduct — every listed property below is non-optional in Swift and therefore required here, except where noted optional.

^_.description: Free-text annotation (e.g. _note). Not decoded by the engine.

billingCurrency.description: The currency a purchase is measured in for THIS card's own earn rules and caps — 'points per currency unit' means per unit of this currency, not per CAD unconditionally. RuleMatcher/Scorer converts the purchase amount into this currency (via PurchaseContext.usdEquivalent, the same field already used for `spendUsdEquivalent` caps) before applying `earn.pointsPerUnit`/`earn.rate`. Independent of `market`: a CAD-market card could in principle bill in USD (none do today), which is why this is its own field rather than derived from `market`.

status.description: Absent means `published` (backward compatible with every pre-2.0 card). `draft` marks a research-grade record that has NOT cleared this catalogue's issuer-confirmed sourcing bar (D3) — RecommendationEngine.recommend and PortfolioAnalyzer refuse to consider a draft card even if it somehow ended up in ownedCardIds, so a draft record can never produce a checkout pick or a keep/cancel number. AcquisitionAnalyzer and the add-card/compare surfaces MAY show draft cards, clearly labelled, because comparing an unowned candidate is lower-stakes than telling someone what to tap. Promoting draft → published is a data edit (re-verify against the issuer, flip the field), never an engine change.

network.description: Network enum. A purchase's acceptedNetworks must contain this or Scorer excludes the card outright (Warning.networkNotAccepted). `discover` added for the US catalogue; no CA card in this catalogue uses it yet. `privateLabel` means the card runs on NO network — a store card accepted only by its own merchant. It is never a member of a purchase's acceptedNetworks, so Scorer would exclude such a card everywhere; the paired `acceptance` object is what makes it scoreable, and the allOf below makes the pair inseparable.

fxRules.description: RuleMatcher.activeFxRule picks the first entry whose effectiveFrom/effectiveTo window covers asOf; later entries let an announced future rate coexist with the current one. Applies when a purchase's currency differs from THIS card's billingCurrency (Scorer compares against billingCurrency, not a hardcoded "CAD") — e.g. a CAD-billing card used on a USD purchase, or (once such a card exists) a USD-billing card used on a CAD purchase.

perTransactionRewardVisibility.description: Free String in Swift, not an enum — these three are the catalogue's current convention, not a type-level constraint.

sources.description: Issuer source URLs. CardProduct has no `sources` property.

stacking.description: Free-text stacking note (e.g. MBNA's five independent $50k caps). Not decoded.

categoryMccReference.description: Human MCC-to-category lookup table (Tangerine). Not decoded; RuleMatcher never reads it.

redemptionFactors.description: Documented redemption boost factors (e.g. Rogers' 1.5x service redemption). Not decoded and not scored in v1 — see the factor's own _note.

credits.description: Optional recurring monetary credits. Absence is only a trustworthy claim of no credits when creditCoverage.status is complete; otherwise it means the card has not been fully reviewed.

lifecycleStatus.description: Optional. Absent means active. Product lifecycle is independent of publication status: a published card can later be withdrawn. A discontinued product is marked 'withdrawn' and kept; it is never deleted and its cardId is never reused, because prediction rows, owner state, and other repos' vendored copies all key on that id.

effectiveTo.description: Optional. The date the product stopped being available — card-level, distinct from earnRule.effectiveTo, which closes one rule's window. Scoring is dated, not boolean: Scorer excludes a withdrawn card only for an asOf after this date, so a historical query still scores the card exactly as it scored at the time. A withdrawn card without this date is excluded on every date.

allOf.$comment: privateLabel implies closed-loop acceptance. A card that runs on no network and does not also say where it IS accepted is excluded everywhere by Scorer — a safe failure, but a useless record. Each `if` carries its own `required`, without which the `if` is vacuously true for a card that omits the key and the clause enforces nothing.

And the converse: closed-loop acceptance implies privateLabel. Declared on a real network it would be a restriction Scorer's openLoop branch silently ignores — a record that states a limit the engine does not enforce.

acceptance is never spelled openLoop. Absence already means openLoop — Scorer coalesces — and an explicit openLoop record would be forced to carry a merchants array that no code path reads, i.e. a stated restriction that is not one. AcceptanceScope keeps the case in Swift and Kotlin as that coalescing default; data may not use it. Together with the two clauses above this reads as one biconditional: network privateLabel <-> acceptance present <-> scope closedLoop.

acceptance.description: How this card is accepted. ABSENT means openLoop, which is every card up to card-contracts@2.4 — so a pre-2.5 catalogue validates unchanged and no existing record moves a byte. Scorer switches on it: openLoop guards on network, closedLoop guards on the purchase's merchantBrand, and an unresolved merchantBrand excludes rather than admits, because silence beats recommending a card that is declined at the till.

scope.description: Mirrors Swift/Kotlin AcceptanceScope. Data may only ever say `closedLoop` — see cardProduct.allOf for why openLoop is unspellable here despite being a legal enum value in code.

merchants.description: Lowercase kebab-case merchant tokens — the same convention RuleMatcher matches merchantInclude against, pinned by CatalogueIntegrityTests.testMerchantBrandTokensAreLowercaseKebabCase. A token that cannot match is a card that can never be picked anywhere.

fee.description: Every field optional in Swift's Fee struct. `annual`/`monthly` are Money — see that def's note on why a bare number was retired.

status.description: Decoded onto FxRule.status but RuleMatcher.activeFxRule selects purely by effectiveFrom/effectiveTo window, never by this field.

announcedAt.description: FxRule has no `announcedAt` property — dropped silently on decode.

freeAllowanceCadPerCalendarMonth.description: When present, Scorer only appends Warning.fxAllowanceAssumed — it does not net the allowance out of fxCost. Name kept CAD-suffixed rather than generalized to Money: every card using this allowance today bills in CAD, and a bare number the engine already ignores past the presence check is not worth a breaking rename in this bump — flagged in card-research-queue.json if a future USD-billing card needs one.

postAllowanceRate.description: Decoded onto FxRule.postAllowanceRate but Scorer never applies it; fxCost is either 0 (allowance present) or the purchase amount (in the card's billing currency) * rate (no allowance), regardless of this value.

sourceType.description: Unlike EarnRule.sourceType, FxRule has NO sourceType property in Swift at all — this key is present in every JSON record but silently dropped on decode.

lastVerifiedAt.description: FxRule has no `lastVerifiedAt` property — dropped silently on decode (contrast CardProduct.lastVerifiedAt and EarnRule.lastVerifiedAt, which are both real).

status.description: Decoded onto EarnRule.status but RuleMatcher.isLive only checks effectiveFrom/effectiveTo/scoredInV1 — this field never gates anything.

capId.description: Use capIds instead to support multi-meter caps.

ownerConditions.description: OPEN vocabulary, same rules as benefits-catalogue.schema.json's family/kind — deliberately NOT a closed enum. RuleMatcher.conditionsResolveTrue switches on the known strings above and treats any unknown id as unresolved (fails closed), so unrecognised ids decode fine and simply never match rather than rejecting the whole catalogue load. A closed enum here is exactly what let amazonEligiblePrimeLinked ship with no RuleMatcher case and no schema complaint; opening it doesn't add a handler, but it stops the schema from claiming one exists. A new id still requires an engine code change to actually gate on.

scoredInV1.description: false excludes the rule from RuleMatcher.isLive regardless of dates. Absent means true. Deprecated: a hand-set boolean carries no machine-readable reason and can't turn itself on when its blocker is fixed. New disabled rules should use requires or outOfScope instead; scoredInV1: false without either is only valid for a rule whose blocker is still unconfirmed (see the rule's _note).

requires.description: Engine capabilities this rule needs, matching EngineCapability's raw values (Engine/Sources/CardCopilotEngine/Models/EngineCapability.swift). RuleMatcher.isLive treats the rule as live only if every named capability is in EngineCapability.supported; an unrecognised or unsupported string skips the rule, same as scoredInV1: false did. Absent means no capability is needed. Turns the rule on automatically the day the named capability ships — no catalogue edit required. Mutually exclusive with outOfScope. `cap.calendarQuarter` and `predicate.ownerSelectedCategory` added 2026-08-26 (both now in EngineCapability.supported) for US rotating/selectable-category cards — see CardState.selectedCategories, which is no longer Tangerine-specific.

reason.description: Why this rule will never be scored by this engine, e.g. an online booking channel PickMe (an at-the-register copilot) does not cover. Human-facing; RuleMatcher.isLive only checks presence, not content.

outOfScope.description: Set when the rule is permanently out of scope — never to be built, as distinct from requires' "not yet". RuleMatcher.isLive always returns false when this is present, regardless of requires or scoredInV1. Mutually exclusive with requires: a rule ruled out permanently must not also declare a capability it is waiting on.

sourceType.description: Decoded onto EarnRule.sourceType (a real Swift property, unlike FxRule's copy of this same key) but never read by any matching or scoring logic.

earn.description: Union on `type`, matching the Earn enum's custom Codable implementation. `pointsPerCad` renamed to `pointsPerUnit` in 2.0 — the rate is always per unit of the card's OWN billingCurrency, not CAD unconditionally (a US card's `pointsPerUnit: 1` means 1 point per USD billed, not per CAD).

premiumCentsPerLitre.description: Earn.centsPerLitre carries no associated value in Swift; the custom decoder reads only `type` for this case and ignores every other key.

oneOf.description: Informational only — Scorer.rawEarn maps this case to -1, and any rule using it (see triangle-fuel-cpl) also sets scoredInV1: false. Needs litres to value, which the catalogue doesn't carry.

predicate.description: Every field optional in Swift's Predicate struct. An empty object {} matches any purchase (base rule).

categories.description: Purchase-category strings, PLUS two engine-defined pseudo-categories RuleMatcher.matches special-cases: "recurring" (checks PurchaseContext.recurringIndicator, ignoring the purchase's actual category) and "ownerSelectedCategory" (checks CardState.selectedCategories — generalized 2026-08-26 from the Tangerine-only "ownerSelectedTangerineCategory"; the old string is still accepted as an alias). Also subject to RuleMatcher.categoryParents expansion — currently only "marriottDirect" implies ["lodging", "travel"], so a predicate listing the parent still matches the more specific purchase category.

mccInclude.description: When present alongside `categories` and the purchase has a known MCC, the MCC must also be in this list. A nil/unknown purchase MCC falls back to matching on category alone (the permissive-fallback path).

merchantExclude.description: Checked before mccInclude/categories — a brand exclusion wins even if the MCC would otherwise qualify (see Costco vs Triangle grocery).

recurringViaNetworkIndicator.description: Decoded onto Predicate.recurringViaNetworkIndicator but RuleMatcher.matches never reads it — the actual recurring gate is the "recurring" pseudo-category checking PurchaseContext.recurringIndicator directly.

measure.description: `spendCad` renamed to `spendNative` in 2.0: the amount is measured in the CARD's own billingCurrency (CAD for a CAD-billing card, USD for a USD-billing card), not CAD unconditionally. `spendUsdEquivalent` is unchanged and stays meaningful even for a USD-billing card's cap stated in a THIRD reference (none exist today, but the case — e.g. Crypto.com's CAD-billing card with a USD-denominated cap — is exactly why the two measures stay distinct rather than collapsing into one).

period.description: Read by PortfolioAnalyzer for monthly-cap reporting and by Swift cap-window projections. MoneyTalks additionally resolves the current server ledger window from this field. `calendarQuarter` added 2026-08-26 (EngineCapability.capCalendarQuarter, now supported) for US rotating-category cards (e.g. 5x groceries up to $1,500/quarter) — the shape this catalogue could not previously express at all.

anchor.description: Decoded onto Cap.anchor (a self-documenting pointer string like "ownerState.scotiaAccountYearAnchorMonth"). MoneyTalks resolves the declared owner-state anchor for account-year ledger windows; Swift cap-window projections resolve the same supported paths.

resetTimeZone.description: Decoded onto Cap.resetTimeZone but the engine never computes a period rollover, so this is never read.

proration.description: Decoded onto Cap.proration but CapMath.split always splits a straddling purchase proportionally, unconditionally — this flag is never branched on.

status.description: Whether issuer material was reviewed comprehensively for standard recurring monetary credits.

unit.description: Required for calendar schedules. A halfYear is Jan-Jun or Jul-Dec.

intervalMonths.description: Required for accountAnniversary and rolling schedules; supports 48- and 54-month reimbursements.

resetTimeZone.description: IANA time-zone identifier when issuer terms establish one. Absence means date-level cadence only; consumers use the owner's local day and must not claim an exact cutoff hour.

cardCredit.description: A standard recurring monetary credit. It may influence checkout only when an issuer-confirmed purchasePredicate matches and owner state proves the credit is enrolled and unused. `value` is the issuer maximum per window, not annualized marketing value or a forecast of use.

value.description: `valueCad` renamed to `value` (Money) in 2.0 — a US card's credit is stated in USD, not converted to CAD at authoring time (Phase 1: never convert USD amounts into CAD fields merely to satisfy the schema).

period.description: Legacy cadence retained for compatibility. New and corrected credits use schedule.

usageTerms.description: Concise issuer-supported restrictions that are material but not safely machine-dispatchable. Never used to broaden purchasePredicate.

sources.description: Issuer pages the amount and period were read from. Required when sourceType is issuerConfirmed (enforced by allOf below) and optional otherwise — an inferred credit has no citation by definition, and requiring one would force either deleting unverified data or inventing a source for it.
